Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:41: Now all these aspects mentioned regarding the greatness of our Maker, Maker of all, that He is great and rules, etc., are explained similarly in Ra'aya Meheimna, portion of Pinchas (Zohar 225a), where the explanation is expanded further - his words: "But the Cause above all, called YHVH, of whom it is said, 'To whom then will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One' (Isaiah 40:25), and 'to whom will you liken God, and what likeness will you compare to Him? I, YHVH, have not changed' - no sin can reach Him to separate His letters, the Yud from the Heh, the Vav from the Heh, for there is no separation; of Him it is said, 'no evil shall dwell with You.' He rules over all and none rules over Him; He grasps everything and none grasps Him; and He is not called YHVH, nor by any of the [other] Names, except through the spreading of His light over them, and when He withdraws from them, He has no name at all of His own from among them. 'Deep, deep, who can find it' - no light can gaze upon Him, for even the supreme Crown, whose light is mighty over all the hosts of heaven above and below and over all the grades, grows dark before Him; of Him it is said, 'He made darkness His hiding place,' and over Chochmah and Binah is 'a thick cloud around Him' - how much more so the other sefirot, how much more the Chayot, how much more the elements, which are dead bodies. He encompasses all the worlds, and none encompasses them on any side, above or below or the four directions, except Him, and none can go outside His domain; He fills all the worlds, and none but He fills them; and there is no god above Him to give Him life, as is said (Nehemiah 9:6) 'and You give life to them all'; and concerning this, Daniel said (5:23) 'and all the inhabitants of the earth are counted as nothing, and He does according to His will with the host of heaven.' He binds and unites each kind to its kind, above and below, and there is no closeness for them in the four elements except through the Holy One, blessed be He, when He is among them" - so far his words. When the discerning reader examines this passage carefully, he will understand the first passage of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning "great and ruling, the root," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:42: And what he said (Zohar I 11b), "and set his desire in that place which is called fear" - the meaning is that all the aforementioned aspects are revealed through it [the place called fear, i.e. Malchut/the Shechinah]. For the Name YHVH is called great and ruler - but where does His greatness become magnified? In it [Malchut], as is written (Psalms 48:2) "Great is the Lord and greatly praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain," as is explained in the portion of Vayikra (Zohar 5a) on this verse - their words: "It is heard that a king without a queen is not a king, is not great, and is not praised."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:43: Further, this matter is explained in the Tikkunim in many places, in particular one place (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 103a) found among us in manuscript - his words: "'and the wise shall shine' (Daniel 12:3) - who are the wise? Those who have the understanding to know the Master of the worlds, who is the Cause above all upper beings, through the Shechinah, of whom it is said (Psalms 118:20) 'This is the gate of the Lord, the righteous shall enter through it' - Sha'ar [gate], when its letters are reversed, spells Esser [ten], comprising the ten sefirot," etc. And he says at the end of the discourse, "and because He is within, the faith of Israel is set in her, for she is bound to all, inward and outward, comprising above and below without end or limit, and therefore he calls her 'the faith of Israel,' and through her the upper and lower beings, and the Cause above all upper beings, become known; and whoever unifies Him through her, it is as though he unifies Him and proclaims Him King over all the upper and lower beings" - so far his words. And likewise in the portion of Terumah (Zohar 158b), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:44: Further, in Ra'aya Meheimna, portion of Pinchas (230a), it is explained even more clearly - his words: "This is the holy kingship [Malchut], which is the image of all, through which the Holy One, blessed be He, looked and created the world and all the creatures He created in the world, and comprises within her the upper and lower worlds without any separation at all, and comprises within her the ten sefirot and all their names, appellations, and expressions of being; and the Cause above all, who is Master over all and there is no god besides Him, is not found among the upper and lower worlds less than in her, since she is the bond of all, the completeness of all, in which He is established, and His kingship rules over all - since the Cause above all is not found among the upper and lower worlds any less than in her, even in one of them - she is called the faith of Israel" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:45: Further, in the Tikkunim in manuscript (Chadash 10a): "and from the side of the three patriarchs, who are called El, Elohim, YHVH - who are 'the great, mighty, and awesome God' - she is called Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, and through these three names she testifies to His being, His divinity, and His power over all the worlds; and from the side of the supernal Mother she is called 'Mother,' [and from the side of] Teshuvah, YHVH, which indicates an appellation - and the [essential] Being [Havayah] of the Master of the worlds is Master of all appellations and all expressions of being, which are appellations for Him, while He Himself is not an appellation; and she is called Ma"H from the side of Chochmah, of whom it is said (Deuteronomy 10:12) 'what [mah] does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear,' for if there is no wisdom there is no fear, and if there is no fear there is no wisdom; and through this Ma"H she testifies concerning the Cause of all the upper beings, for they do not know what [mah] He is" - so far his words. Here it is that the revelation of His divinity and power, blessed be He, comes through her [Malchut]; if so, it is fitting that "great and ruling, the root and source," through which everything is revealed, be ascribed to her as well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:46: Likewise in the Scriptures we find greatness and dominion ascribed also to this attribute [Malchut]: "Great is our Lord and abundant in power," etc. So too what is explained in the Zohar, portion of Bereishit (19a), on the verse (Lamentations 3:23) "they are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness," see there. And likewise (Psalms 145:13) "Your kingdom is a kingdom of all worlds, and Your dominion is in every generation." The aspect of "root and source of all worlds" is also stated in the phrase "Your kingdom is a kingdom of all worlds," and its meaning is understood by the secret that "the end of the deed is first in thought" - see the Tikkunim (11a) concerning (Proverbs 8:22) "The Lord made me as the beginning of His way," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:47: There is no need to elaborate further on this aspect, for since YHVH is the root and source of all worlds, as I explained above, and the revelation of His action through them is, as I explained above, called Gedulah, Gevurah, Tiferet, which testify to His divinity, etc., and "everything is as nothing before Him" - this aspect too is contained within it [Malchut].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:48: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this on the verse (I Kings 5:10) "and Solomon's wisdom grew," etc. - he said there, in the portion of Vayechi (Zohar 223a): "the moon [the Shechinah] stood before a thousand great mountains, and they were all as a single breath before her; a thousand great rivers were hers, and in a single sip she swallowed them" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:49: Likewise, in the portion of Pinchas (Zohar 240b) - his words: "Rather, it is a secret, for there is a beast [Behemah] that crouches over a thousand mountains, and it consumes a thousand mountains every day, and they are all called 'beasts.' Concerning this we learn that 'there is a beast that eats beasts.' From where did they come? From fire, and this beast licks them all up in a single lick, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:24) 'for the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.' And all the waters of the Jordan, full for six years, she made into a single swallow, as it is said (Job 40:23) 'he trusts that he can draw up the Jordan into his mouth'" - so far his words. On the secret of this "beast" hangs the arousal of the lower worlds, whose essence lies in the secret of Ba"N from Binyamin, which is the secret of "and let not oil be lacking on your head," as I explained in the Gate of Love, beginning of chapter 5.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:50: It may be said that these four aspects mentioned - "great, and ruling, root," etc., "and everything is as nothing before Him" - correspond to the four letters of YHVH, and are revealed through the Name Adnut [Adonai/Malchut]; there is no room to elaborate further.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:51: All the aspects of fear explained as resulting from His being great and ruling, the root, etc., are all present in the Shechinah in relation to the lower beings. For from her side come the souls of Israel, and likewise the life-force of all the lower beings; and when a person dies, the soul returns to her, as is explained in the portion of Vayechi (Zohar 217b) - his words: "Rabbi Yehudah said: at the time when a person's feet become bound together and his days draw near, that day is called 'the day of the Lord,' to return his spirit to Him. We learn in that teaching that this holy crown [Malchut] is entrusted with his spirit; and who is she? As is written (Psalms 90:10) 'the days of our years among them are seventy years' - and she is the seventh crown of all" - so far his words. Therefore one must fear her, for it is in her power to remove the soul in an instant; this is (Daniel 5:23) "and to the God in whose hand is your breath, and all your ways, [you have not glorified]." And likewise (Job 12:10) "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing and the breath of all mankind" - for the Shechinah is called "hand," and the explanation of this verse will be given in the next chapter, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:52: Also the aspect we explained, that one ought not to sin and be ungrateful for all the good the Holy One, blessed be He, has done for him - this aspect too is present in her, for she is the mother who raises us; one must fear her judgment and love her for her mercy, and this is the fear that leads to love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:53: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this aspect in the Pekudin printed in the portion of Va'etchanan (Zohar 263b) - his words: "The commandment to fear, in a general way and in a particular way, as we have established, is because a person must fear before the Holy One, blessed be He, always; and through fear he will keep to His ways, and 'fear' is [also] the name of a place called Fear, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:58) 'to fear this glorious and awesome Name, the Lord your God' - because there dwells the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is true fear, to fear Him; and this is the secret of what is written 'and you shall fear My sanctuary' - in this fear dwells the fiery lash to punish the wicked who do not keep the commandments of the Torah. Therefore, in a general way one must fear, and afterward in a particular way, when a person knows what the fear of the Lord truly is - this is the loving fear, which is the essence and foundation for loving the Holy One, blessed be He; after this fear, he goes on to keep all the commandments of the Torah, so that a person becomes a faithful servant to the Holy One, blessed be He, as fitting fear requires" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:54: My teacher, peace be upon him, wrote concerning the phrase "when he knows what the fear of the Lord truly is," that the meaning is that he should fear lest his sins cause the Shechinah to be separated from the Name YHVH, which is Tiferet, and he should say in his heart, "How could I, through my sins, cause the love of intimate companions and friends to be severed, and thereby become a talebearer who separates close friends?" This aspect of fear is the fear that leads to love, for it is not enough that he not sin, but he should also strive to perform mitzvot in order to unify and draw the love closer. However, in the earlier fear, which is fear of punishment - the one who fears performs a mitzvah because he fears excision [karet], such as not to neglect the mitzvah of circumcision, for which one is liable to karet, or not to eat forbidden fat, for which one is liable to karet - certainly such a person, who fears only the punishment, will not strive to fulfill the commandments [beyond what avoids punishment]. This is the sum of his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 1:55: Now, for the reason we stated above, that His being great and ruling, etc., is revealed through the Shechinah, Rashbi, peace be upon him, said there in the portion of Bereishit (Zohar I 11b) - his words: "And therefore, the place called 'the fear of the Lord' is called 'the beginning' [reishit], and therefore this commandment is included here, for it is the root and foundation for all the other commandments of the Torah; whoever keeps fear keeps everything, whoever does not keep fear does not keep the commandments of the Torah, for this is the gate of everything; and therefore it is written 'Bereishit' - that is, fear - 'God created the heavens and the earth'" - so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:1: Among the things that arouse the inner fear discussed in the previous chapter, one is a person's contemplation, with his intellect, of the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, for their sheer greatness inspires fear, as David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 66:3) "Say to God, how awesome are Your works." So too Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, in the portion "And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear" (Deuteronomy 10:12,14), says, "Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens and the highest heavens, the earth and all that is in it" - it appears that this is one of the things that arouse fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:2: This matter is explained in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, and in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, and we must quote their words, of blessed memory, in order to arouse the heart to fear. In Tractate Chagigah (13a) - their words: "From the earth to the firmament is a journey of five hundred years, and the thickness of the firmament is a journey of five hundred years, and so between each firmament and the next; above them are the Holy Chayot [Living Creatures] - the legs of the Chayot correspond to all of them [combined], the ankles of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the thighs of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the knees of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the loins of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the bodies of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the necks of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the heads of the Chayot correspond to all of them, the horns of the Chayot correspond to all of them; above them is the Throne of Glory - the legs of the Throne of Glory correspond to all of them, the Throne of Glory itself corresponds to all of them; the King, the living and eternal God, exalted and lofty, dwells upon them" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:3: And in the portion of Beshalach (56b), on the verse (Exodus 15:4) "Pharaoh's chariots and his army He cast into the sea," this matter is explained further - his words: "Rabbi Yitzchak opened (Jeremiah 10:12-13) 'At the sound of His giving forth a multitude of waters in the heavens,' etc. We have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He, made seven firmaments, and in each and every firmament stars are fixed and run their course, and above all of them is Aravot; and each firmament in its expanse is two hundred years' journey, and its height five hundred years' journey, and between one firmament and the next, five hundred years' journey; and this Aravot is fifteen hundred years' journey in length and fifteen hundred years' journey in breadth, and from its splendor all those firmaments shine. And we have learned that above Aravot is the span of the Holy Chayot, whose height is as great as all of them combined, and the ankles of the Chayot are as great as all of them," etc. - so far what is explained in the Talmud, so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:4: Further (58a), in the same portion: we learn that his name is Hadarniel, and he is superior to the other angels by sixty myriad parasangs, and his voice travels through two hundred thousand firmaments that whirl in white fire - so far his words. This is the second angel that Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, encountered when he ascended to receive the Torah; and Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, feared this angel until he mentioned the Name of Seventy-Two, and when this angel heard the letters of the Name, he trembled and drew near to him. And the passage continues afterward: and he went with him until they reached the mighty fire of an angel named Sandalfon; and we learn that Sandalfon is superior to his other companions by five hundred years, and he stands behind the curtain of his Master and binds crowns from the requests in Israel's prayers, and when this crown reaches the head of the Holy King, He accepts the prayers of Israel, and all the hosts and camps tremble and say, "Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of His Shechinah's abode." Hadarniel said to Moses, "I cannot go with you, lest the mighty fire of Sandalfon burn me"; at that moment Moses trembled, until the Holy One, blessed be He, took hold of Moses and set him before Him," etc. - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:5: Now, from the greatness of the servants, the greatness of the Master becomes known; for if the rank of His angels is so great, how much more so is the greatness of His attributes in Atzilut, and how much more still is His own greatness, blessed be He, which has no end or limit - especially for those who see the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, as he explained in the Idra of Naso (127b-145a) concerning the multitude of the worlds in Atzilut. They have seen the works of the Lord and His wonders. And it is said in the Tikkunim (135b): "the supernal crown, though it is primordial light, pure light, polished light, is dark before the Cause of causes" - so far, as relevant to us. It is in respect of this great illumination, which has no limit, that the Infinite is called "great," as I explained above (chapter 1), in passing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:6: Now, when a person contemplates His works, blessed be He, he will fear and be humbled by His greatness, and feel shame before Him, and not transgress His commandment. So said Jonah the prophet (Jonah 1:9) "and I fear the Lord, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land." It appears that the fear comes from His works, which display His greatness. So too David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 8:4-5) "When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and stars which You have set in place - what is man that You are mindful of him?" So too Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 16:7) "and what are we," for we do not enter the category of created beings at all in comparison to His greatness, blessed be He, as is said (Daniel 4:32) "and all the inhabitants of the earth are counted as nothing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:7: Further, a second aspect for arousing fear, close to the one just mentioned: a person's contemplation, with his knowledge, of the signs and wonders renewed in the world. Thus Israel, when they saw the great miracle done for them at the sea, fear is stated of them, as is said (Exodus 14:31) "and Israel saw the great hand which the Lord wrought upon Egypt, and the people feared the Lord," etc. So too the Psalmist said (Psalms 65:7-9) "who establishes the mountains by His strength, girded with might, who stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves and the tumult of the peoples; and those who dwell at the ends of the earth are afraid of Your signs; You make the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice," etc., and the other wonders and signs of the Lord, blessed be He, mentioned in that psalm.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:8: Further, a third aspect for arousing fear, also close to the one just mentioned: a person's contemplation of the abundant goodness of the Creator toward him. This is what the prophet said (Malachi 1:6) "and if I am a father, where is My honor," etc., "where is My fear." This is because it is a father's way to do good and show mercy to his son, and if the son sins, the father chastises him, as in (Proverbs 1:8) "hear, my son, the discipline of your father." This is what the prophet Jeremiah, peace be upon him, said (Jeremiah 5:24) "and they did not say in their hearts, let us fear the Lord our God, who gives rain, the early and the late rain in its season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of the harvest... your iniquities have turned these away, and your sins have withheld the good from you." Here it is explicitly fear from the aspect of goodness, as it says "let us fear... who gives rain," etc.; "your iniquities have turned these away" - here are the sufferings. But the fear is not on account of the sufferings; rather, since it is the father's way to do good and show mercy, one must fear lest he himself be the cause of his Father dealing harshly with him and withholding good from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:9: In respect of this aspect of fear, one can explain what is explained in the Tikkunim (Chadash 129a) and in the Zohar, portion of Naso (122b): the letter Yud of Yirah [fear] - this is upon a person's head, and from it enters fear into a person's heart, to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, and to guard himself from transgressing the commandments - so far his words. This is also explained in the Midrash Ruth from the Zohar (82b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:10: In respect of this aspect of fear, one can explain the verse (Deuteronomy 28:58) "to fear this glorious [nichbad] and awesome Name," etc., for there is an aspect in which He is called "glorious" [nichbad] in respect of the goodness that flows from Him, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:11: Kavod [glory/honor] is explained in the Zohar, portion of Pekudei (Zohar 221b), as denoting illumination, on the verse (Isaiah 11:10) "the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner for the peoples, to him shall the nations turn, and his resting place shall be glory [kavod]" - his words: "'and his resting place shall be glory' - his resting place is the Holy Temple, and 'glory' - for at that time it will be called 'glory,' as is written (ibid. 30:26) 'and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold,' and the resting place of that root of Jesse shall be called 'the glory of the Lord,' which cannot be counted or reckoned in number forever" - so far, as relevant to us. Here it is explicitly stated that when it is called "glory," it means that it rises to a level of great illumination such that the light of the moon becomes like the light of the sun, and then it no longer stands within measure and reckoning as it does when it is below, as is written (Song of Songs 7:5) "your eyes are like the pools in Cheshbon, by the gate of Bat Rabim," as is explained in the portion of Pinchas (Zohar 220b); and it is likewise explained in the portion of Bereishit (8a), on the verse (Psalms 19:2) "the heavens declare the glory of God," that "glory" denotes illumination and importance, see there. And we find in the verses that "glory" means light: in Isaiah (60:1) "and the glory of the Lord has shone upon you," and in Ezekiel (43:2) "and the earth shone with His glory," and in the Torah (Exodus 40:34) "and the glory of the Lord filled the Tabernacle," and likewise (Leviticus 9:6) "and the glory of the Lord shall appear to you," and many like these.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:12: It may also be that "glory" is called "light" because the Targum renders "kavod" as "yekar" [preciousness], and it is written (Zechariah 14:6) "and it shall come to pass in that day that there shall be no light, the precious ones [yekarot] shall congeal" - meaning bright light; for "precious" denotes importance, and there is no importance in light except from its brightness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:13: Likewise, when it is said (Isaiah 11:10) "and his resting place shall be glory," "glory" means that it rises in rank and importance - and what is the importance above, in Atzilut? The brightness of its light, that the light of the moon should become like the light of the sun.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:14: Likewise, in Ra'aya Meheimna, portion of Pinchas (Zohar 225b), it is explained that what Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 33:18) "Show me now Your glory" was concerning the supernal crown [Keter] - his words: "And therefore the measure of a sukkah is not less than ten [handbreadths], for it [corresponds to] Malchut, the tenth of all the grades, and not more than twenty, for that is the supernal crown, which the eye cannot govern. Concerning the supernal glory Moses said, 'Show me now Your glory,' and the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him, 'You cannot see My face,' for there is no 'glory' [kavod] without a Kaf [i.e., 'like' - meaning only an image, a reflection, can be seen]" - so far, as relevant to us. We thus find that "glory" is called such through the illumination of the bright light coming from above, as it says "there is no glory without a Kaf." This clarifies the wording of the passage above, which said "it is called the glory of the Lord which cannot be counted," etc., and similarly (Exodus 33:22) "and it shall be, while My glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft," etc.; and in Job (19:9) "He has stripped my glory from me," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:15: We find, then, that when it says "the glorious Name" [HaShem HaNichbad], it means that He is the source of illumination for all created beings, for they all receive light and abundance from YHVH, as I explained in the previous chapter; and this is what I explained, that "glorious" [nichbad] denotes the goodness that flows from Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:16: With this we understand what is said in the Zohar, portion of Vayelech (241b), that one who intends [in prayer] to unify the Name - of him it is said, "for those who honor Me, I will honor" [Ki Mechabdai Achabed]. The reason is that through his good intention he draws additional illumination above, as is explained there regarding the manner of unification, and therefore from there illumination is drawn to his soul in the World to Come, and this is his "glory" [kavod].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:17: "And awesome" [HaNora] - explained by what was stated above in the passage we quoted from the portion of Beshalach, that even among the angels, the others fear to approach the one who is greater than his fellow. Likewise (Exodus 34:30) "and they were afraid to come near him" is said of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, because of the shining of his face. And it is said in the Zohar, portion of Beshalach (58a), that when Israel sinned with the calf, the Holy One, blessed be He, took from Moses a thousand portions of that splendor, and from the splendor that remained in him, Moses' face shone; and if from what remained in him they could not gaze upon his face, how much more so [could they not gaze upon] what was removed from him - so far, as relevant to us. Similarly it is said concerning "and awesome": since He is "glorious" in the manner we explained, it follows that He is "awesome," for all the hosts above fear to approach Him because of His infinite light, lest their very existence be annulled - along the lines of what is explained in the Sefer Brit Menuchah concerning the "graves of craving," that there they buried the people who craved, for any angel who desires and craves to rise above his own rank has his existence annulled; and this is the matter of the "burial" that comes from craving, which is desire.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:18: Along these lines is the explanation of (Ecclesiastes 12:13) "Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man" [kol ha'adam]. The matter is that there is an "Adam" of Atzilut, an "Adam" of Beriah, an "Adam" of Yetzirah, and an "Adam" of Asiyah, as is explained in the Tikkunim (41b); and all these aspects of Adam have their own fear, that the Adam of Beriah should not enter to look and gaze inward at a level above his own, which is in Atzilut, and likewise for the others. Not only this, but even within Atzilut itself it is explained in the Tikkunim (119a) that there is no sefirah that is not called "Adam," and all the aspects of Adam within Atzilut have this fear, so that even Keter, in a certain sense, has this fear, since it is emanated and it is dark before the Cause of causes - it fears the Cause above all causes. This is [the meaning of] "this is the whole of man" - meaning, all the aforementioned aspects of Adam have fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:19: Along these lines my teacher, peace be upon him, explained in the book Tefillah LeMoshe these verses (Psalms 48:5-7): "For behold, the kings assembled, they passed by together; they saw, so they were astounded, they were dismayed, they hurried away; trembling seized them there, pangs as of a woman in labor." For all this happens at the time of the ascent of the [supernal] Palaces upward, and upon their ascent there, "they saw, so they were astounded," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:20: Further, one can explain "the glorious and the awesome" in another way, close to the manner stated: we find that the soul is called "glory" [kavod], as it is said (ibid. 30:13) "so that my glory may sing praise to You and not be silent," and likewise (ibid. 16:9) "therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices." This is because a person's glory, and what illuminates within him, is his soul; if so, "the glorious one" means that He is the source for all souls - and not only the souls of the lower beings, but He is the source of illumination that illuminates all the upper worlds, and He is a soul within them; and just as the soul illuminates the body, so is He, blessed be He, the source of the soul for all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:21: "And the awesome" accordingly means that, since "in His hand is the soul of every living thing and the breath of all mankind" (Job 12:10), one must fear Him, for it is in His power to remove the soul in an instant, and "all flesh would perish together," as is written (Daniel 5:23) "and to the God in whose hand is your breath, and all your ways, [you have not glorified Him]." In this same respect, all the hosts above also fear Him, since their flow and vitality depend on Him; and this is [the meaning of] "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing" - namely, the hosts above, who live and endure forever, their vitality depending on Him, blessed be He, and "every living thing" includes, up to the very highest, the whole reality of the emanated beings. "And the breath of all mankind" refers to the physical, lower beings in the lower Asiyah, and therefore the term "flesh" is used for them, because death and dissolution rule over them; but concerning the upper beings, in whom there is no death, it says "every living thing," for they all live from His vitality, blessed be He, as is said (Nehemiah 9:6) "and You give life to them all."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:22: Further, we find that Scripture uses the word "kavod" for praise and glorification, as in (Psalms 29:9) "and in His Temple all say 'Glory'" - meaning the praise and glorification said to the Lord, blessed be He. And in Ra'aya Meheimna, portion of Kedoshim (81b), it is explained that "kavod" has the numerical value of 32, referring to the thirty-two paths of wisdom. It is known, as stated in Sefer Yetzirah, that with the thirty-two paths of wisdom, which are the thirty-two "gods" [elohim] mentioned in the account of Creation, [God] engraved YH YHVH Tzeva'ot His universe. The meaning is that through these thirty-two paths the creation of all the worlds took place, which is the matter of the whole account of Creation; and the thirty-two paths are ascribed to the word "kavod," because the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is revealed to us through His works and the great creatures He created, as I explained at the beginning of this chapter, and through this we honor and praise Him, as it is said (Isaiah 43:7) "all that is called by My Name, and for My glory I have created it" - the explanation of "for My glory I have created it" being that it should honor and praise Me, and for this I created it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:23: Further, "the glorious" may mean, as explained in Ra'aya Meheimna, which we quoted above at the end of chapter 1, concerning (ibid. 6:3) "the whole earth is full of His glory" - this refers to the glory of His divinity, blessed be He, revealed to us through the spreading of the worlds from cause to effect, as it says, "for if His light did not spread over all creatures, how would they come to know Him, and how would 'the whole earth is full of His glory' be fulfilled?" And the glory of the Godhead is revealed through the letter Kaf of Keter, for "there is no glory without a Kaf," as I explained above; and afterward the light is clothed through the thirty-two paths of wisdom, which are the ten utterances and the twenty-two letters, as is explained in the Tikkunim (78b), and through the thirty-two paths, by which the whole account of Creation was accomplished, "the whole earth is full of His glory" is fulfilled. In this respect YHVH is called "glorious," for through Him all was created through the thirty-two paths, and He comprises them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 2:24: Likewise, He is "glorious" in the sense that He is bound forever and comprises the glory of the supernal Godhead through the Crown, which is the Kaf, as is explained in the Tikkunim, which we quoted above in chapter 1: the Name is not called by the unity of the four letters except through the unity of the Cause of causes who unifies them, and through this "glory" it spreads downward to the lower beings, in the secret of "the whole earth is full of His glory," which I explained in chapter 1. With this explanation, all the interpretations we have given concerning "the glorious" converge upon a single path.
